title.zh: 卷21 列傳第13 尉遲迥 王謙 司馬消難
title.en: Volume 21 Biographies 13: Wei Chijiong; Wang Qian; Sima Xiaonan
title.raw: 卷21 列傳第13 尉遲迥 王謙 司馬消難 Volume 21 Biographies 13: Wei Chijiong; Wang Qian; Sima Xiaonan

sentences.zh: 尉遲迥 王謙 司馬消難

translations.literal: Wei Chijiong; Wang Qian; Sima Xiaonan
translations.idiomatic: Wei Chijiong (Yuchi Jiong); Wang Qian; Sima Xiaonan

sentences.zh: 尉遲迥字薄居羅，代人也。

translations.literal: Yuchi Jiong, styled Boruoluo, was a man of Dai.
translations.idiomatic: Yuchi Jiong, styled Boruoluo, came from Dai.

sentences.zh: 其先，魏之別種，號尉遲部，因而姓焉。

translations.literal: His forebears were a separate branch of Wei; they were called the Yuchi tribe, and from that they took their surname.
translations.idiomatic: His clan was a separate branch of the Wei people, known as the Yuchi tribe, and took that name as their surname.

sentences.zh: 父俟兜，性弘裕，有鑒識，尚太祖姊昌樂大長公主，生迥及綱。

translations.literal: His father Sidou was broad-minded and generous, had discernment and judgment, married Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai's elder sister, the Grand Princess of Changle, and fathered Jiong and Gang.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sidou was open-handed and perceptive; he married Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai's elder sister, the Grand Princess of Changle, and fathered Jiong and Gang.

sentences.zh: 俟兜病且卒，呼二子，撫其首曰：「汝等並有貴相，但恨吾不見爾，各宜勉之。」

translations.literal: When Sidou was ill and near death, he called his two sons, stroked their heads, and said: "You both have the look of great men, but I regret I shall not see you reach it; each of you must strive hard."
translations.idiomatic: As Sidou lay dying, he called his two sons, stroked their heads, and said: "You both bear the marks of greatness, but I shall not live to see it—each of you must do your utmost."

sentences.zh: 迥少聰敏，美容儀。

translations.literal: Jiong from youth was clever and quick, with fine bearing and appearance.
translations.idiomatic: From boyhood Yuchi Jiong was clever and handsome.

sentences.zh: 及長，有大志，好施愛士。

translations.literal: When he grew up, he had great ambition and loved to bestow favors and cherish men of talent.
translations.idiomatic: As a man he nursed great ambitions and was generous and fond of nurturing talent.

sentences.zh: 稍遷大丞相帳內都督。

translations.literal: He was gradually transferred to commander within the Grand Chancellor's tent staff.
translations.idiomatic: He rose by stages to commander in Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai's headquarters staff.

sentences.zh: 尚魏文帝女金明公主，拜駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: He married Princess Jinming, daughter of Emperor Wen of Wei, and was appointed commandant of the imperial son-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: He married Princess Jinming, daughter of Emperor Wen of Wei, and was made commandant of the imperial son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 從太祖復弘農，破沙苑，皆有功。

translations.literal: He followed Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai in recovering Hongnong and breaking Shayuan, and in both had merit.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai in retaking Hongnong and winning at Shayuan, earning distinction in both.

sentences.zh: 累遷尚書左僕射，兼領軍將軍。

translations.literal: By cumulative promotion he became left vice director of the masters of writing, concurrently holding the post of commander-in-chief of the army.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to left vice director of the masters of writing and concurrently commander-in-chief of the army.

sentences.zh: 迥通敏有幹能，雖任兼文武，頗允時望。

translations.literal: Jiong was penetrating and quick, with practical ability; though his duties combined civil and military roles, he quite fulfilled the hopes of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Yuchi Jiong was quick-witted and capable; though his duties spanned civil and military affairs, he largely lived up to what the age expected of him.

sentences.zh: 太祖以此深委仗焉。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai for this reason deeply entrusted affairs to him.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai therefore placed deep trust in him.

sentences.zh: 後拜大將軍。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed grand general.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made grand general.

sentences.zh: 侯景之渡江，梁元帝時鎮江陵，旣以內難方殷，請脩鄰好。

translations.literal: When Hou Jing crossed the Yangtze, Emperor Yuan of Liang was then garrisoning Jiangling; since internal troubles were pressing, he requested to restore neighborly relations.
translations.idiomatic: When Hou Jing crossed the Yangtze, Emperor Yuan of Liang held Jiangling; with civil war raging at home, he sought to mend relations with the north.

sentences.zh: 其弟武陵王紀，在蜀稱帝，率衆東下，將攻之。

translations.literal: His younger brother, Prince of Wuling Xiao Ji, in Shu proclaimed himself emperor, led troops east, and was about to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Xiao Ji, Prince of Wuling, had declared himself emperor in Shu and was marching east to attack him.

sentences.zh: 梁元帝大懼，乃移書請救，又請伐蜀。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan of Liang was greatly afraid; he thereupon sent a letter requesting rescue, and also requested a campaign against Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan of Liang was terrified; he sent appeals for aid and also asked for an expedition against Shu.

sentences.zh: 太祖曰：「蜀可圖矣。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai said: "Shu can now be taken.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai said: "Shu can be taken now.

sentences.zh: 取蜀制梁，在茲一舉。

translations.literal: To take Shu and control Liang—here in this one move it lies."
translations.idiomatic: Seize Shu and you control Liang—all hangs on this one stroke."

sentences.zh: 」乃與羣公會議，諸將多有異同。

translations.literal: " He thereupon met with the assembled lords in council; among the generals many had differing views.
translations.idiomatic: " He then convened the senior lords; the generals were divided.

sentences.zh: 唯迥以為紀旣盡銳東下，蜀必空虛，王師臨之，必有征無戰。

translations.literal: Only Jiong held that since Ji had already sent his best troops east, Shu must be empty; when the royal army arrived, there would surely be a campaign but no battle.
translations.idiomatic: Only Yuchi Jiong argued that with Ji's best troops already marching east, Shu would be hollow; once the imperial army arrived, victory would come without a fight.

sentences.zh: 太祖深以為然，謂迥曰：「伐蜀之事，一以委汝，計將安出？

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai deeply agreed, and said to Jiong: "The matter of campaigning against Shu I wholly entrust to you—what plan do you propose?"
translations.idiomatic: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai strongly agreed and asked Yuchi Jiong: "The Shu campaign is entirely in your hands—what is your plan?"

sentences.zh: 」迥曰：「蜀與中國隔絕百有餘年，恃其山川險阻，不虞我師之至。

translations.literal: " Jiong said: "Shu and the Central States have been cut off for more than a hundred years; relying on its mountains and rivers, steep and blocked, it does not expect our army's arrival.
translations.idiomatic: " Yuchi Jiong said: "Shu has been isolated from the heartland for over a century; trusting in its rugged terrain, it will not expect our army.

sentences.zh: 宜以精甲銳騎，星夜襲之。

translations.literal: We should use picked armor and sharp cavalry and strike by night as if borne on stars."
translations.idiomatic: Send elite infantry and swift cavalry and fall upon them in a night march."

sentences.zh: 平路則倍道兼行，險途則緩兵漸進，出其不意，沖其腹心。

translations.literal: On level roads we should double the stages and march day and night; on dangerous paths we should slow the army and advance step by step; take them unawares and thrust at their vitals.
translations.idiomatic: On open roads, force the pace; on difficult ground, advance in measured steps—catch them off guard and drive at the heart of the province.

sentences.zh: 蜀人旣駭官軍之臨速，必望風不守矣。

translations.literal: Once the people of Shu are alarmed that the official army has come so swiftly, they will surely see the wind and not hold their posts."
translations.idiomatic: Once the Shu people see how fast the imperial army has come, they will collapse at the first rumor of its approach."

sentences.zh: 」於是乃令迥督開府元珍、乙弗亞、

translations.literal: " He thereupon ordered Jiong to supervise opening-office Yuan Zhen, Yifu Ya,
translations.idiomatic: " He then put Yuchi Jiong in command of opening-office Yuan Zhen, Yifu Ya,

translations.literal: (wan)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: wan]

sentences.zh: 俟呂陵始、叱奴興、綦連〔雄〕、宇文升等六軍，甲士一萬二千，騎萬疋，伐蜀。

translations.literal: Hou Lüling Shi, Chinu Xing, Qilian [Xiong], Yuwen Sheng, and others—six armies—with twelve thousand armored soldiers and ten thousand horses, to campaign against Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Lüling Shi, Chinu Xing, Qilian Xiong, Yuwen Sheng, and others in six armies—twelve thousand armored foot and ten thousand horse—to invade Shu.

sentences.zh: 以魏廢帝二年春，自散關由固道出白馬，趣晉壽，開平林舊道。

translations.literal: In spring of the second year of the Deposed Emperor of Wei, from San Pass by the Gudao route through White Horse, he hastened toward Jinshou and opened the old Pinglin road.
translations.idiomatic: In spring of the Deposed Emperor of Wei's second year he marched from San Pass by the Gudao route through White Horse toward Jinshou and reopened the old Pinglin road.

sentences.zh: 前軍臨劔閣，紀安州刺史樂廣，以州先降。

translations.literal: The vanguard reached Jian Pass; Ji's governor of An Province, Yue Guang, surrendered the province first.
translations.idiomatic: The vanguard reached Jian Pass; Yue Guang, Ji's governor of An Province, surrendered first.

sentences.zh: 紀梁州刺史楊乾運時鎮潼州，又降。

translations.literal: Ji's governor of Liang Province, Yang Qianyun, was then garrisoning Tong Province and also surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Qianyun, Ji's governor of Liang Province then holding Tong Province, surrendered as well.

sentences.zh: 六月，迥至潼州，大饗將士，引之而西。

translations.literal: In the sixth month Jiong reached Tong Province, feasted the officers and soldiers greatly, and led them west.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month Yuchi Jiong reached Tong Province, held a great feast for his troops, and marched west.

sentences.zh: 紀益州刺史蕭撝不敢戰，遂嬰城自守。

translations.literal: Ji's governor of Yi Province, Xiao Hui, did not dare to fight and thereupon closed the city and held firm.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Hui, Ji's governor of Yi Province, dared not give battle and shut himself inside the city walls.

sentences.zh: 進軍圍之。

translations.literal: The army advanced and besieged it.
translations.idiomatic: The army advanced and laid siege.

sentences.zh: 初，紀至巴郡，聞迥來侵，遣譙淹回師，為撝外援。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Ji reached Ba commandery and heard that Jiong was coming to invade, he dispatched Qiao Yan to turn his army back as external support for Hui.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Ji reached Ba commandery and learned that Yuchi Jiong was invading, he sent Qiao Yan back with his army to reinforce Hui.

sentences.zh: 迥分遣元珍、乙弗亞等以輕騎破之，遂降。

translations.literal: Jiong separately dispatched Yuan Zhen, Yifu Ya, and others with light cavalry to defeat him, and he thereupon surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Yuchi Jiong sent Yuan Zhen, Yifu Ya, and others with light cavalry to break them, and Qiao Yan surrendered.

sentences.zh: 撝前後戰數十合，皆為迥所破。

translations.literal: Hui fought several dozen engagements before and after, and in all was defeated by Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Hui fought dozens of engagements and was beaten every time by Yuchi Jiong.

sentences.zh: 撝與紀子宜都王肅，及其文武官屬，詣軍門請見，迥以禮接之。

translations.literal: Hui together with his son, Prince Su of Yidu, and his civil and military officials and attendants came to the camp gate to request audience; Jiong received them with ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Xiao Hui came with his son, Prince Su of Yidu, and his civil and military staff to the camp gate to surrender; Yuchi Jiong received them with full courtesy.

sentences.zh: 其吏人等，各令復業。

translations.literal: Their clerks and common people, each was ordered to return to his occupation.
translations.idiomatic: Clerks and commoners alike were told to return to their trades.

sentences.zh: 唯收僮隸及儲積以賞將士。

translations.literal: Only bond servants and stored provisions were taken to reward the officers and soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Only bond servants and stored provisions were seized to reward the troops.

sentences.zh: 號令嚴肅，軍無私焉。

translations.literal: Orders and commands were strict and solemn; the army had no private gain.
translations.idiomatic: Discipline was strict and the army took no private plunder.

sentences.zh: 詔迥為大都督、益潼等十八州諸軍事、益州刺史。

translations.literal: An edict appointed Jiong grand commander, military affairs of the eighteen provinces including Yi and Tong, and governor of Yi Province.
translations.idiomatic: An edict made Yuchi Jiong grand commander over military affairs in eighteen provinces including Yi and Tong, and governor of Yi Province.

sentences.zh: 以平蜀功，封一子為公。

translations.literal: For the merit of pacifying Shu, one son was enfeoffed duke.
translations.idiomatic: For pacifying Shu, one of his sons was enfeoffed duke.

sentences.zh: 自劔閣以南，得承制封拜及黜陟。

translations.literal: From Jian Pass southward, he was authorized to act by imperial mandate in enfeoffing, appointing, and promoting or demoting officials.
translations.idiomatic: South of Jian Pass he was empowered to enfeoff, appoint, promote, and dismiss officials by delegated imperial authority.

sentences.zh: 迥乃明賞罰，布恩威，綏緝新邦，經略未附，夷夏懷而歸之。

translations.literal: Jiong thereupon made rewards and punishments clear, spread favor and awe, soothed and gathered the new territory, planned strategy toward those not yet submitted, and both barbarians and Chinese cherished him and came to him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuchi Jiong then made rewards and punishments clear, combined kindness with authority, settled the newly conquered lands, reached out to those still unsubmitted, and won over both barbarian and Chinese alike.

sentences.zh: 迥性至孝，色養不怠。

translations.literal: Jiong by nature was utterly filial; in cheerful attendance for his parents' comfort he never slackened.
translations.idiomatic: Yuchi Jiong was profoundly filial and never slackened in keeping his mother's spirits up.

sentences.zh: 身雖在外，所得四時甘脆，必先薦奉，然後敢嘗。

translations.literal: Though his person was abroad, whenever he obtained seasonal delicacies, he always offered them first in sacrifice and only then dared to taste them.
translations.idiomatic: Though he served far from home, any seasonal delicacy he received he first offered to his mother before tasting it himself.

sentences.zh: 大長公主年高多病，迥往在京師，每退朝參候起居，憂悴形于容色。

translations.literal: The Grand Princess was advanced in years and often ill; when Jiong was in the capital, after each court session he would attend and inquire after her health, and worry and emaciation showed in his countenance.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Princess was old and often ill; when Yuchi Jiong was in the capital he visited her after every court session, and his face showed how worn he was with worry.

sentences.zh: 大長公主每為之和顏進食，以寧迥心。

translations.literal: The Grand Princess each time for his sake would compose her face and urge food upon him, to settle Jiong's heart.
translations.idiomatic: Each time the Grand Princess would soften her manner and press food on him to ease his mind.

sentences.zh: 太祖知其至性，徵迥入朝，以慰其母意。

translations.literal: Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai knew his utmost filial nature, summoned Jiong to court, to comfort his mother's heart.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing his deep filial devotion, Grand Progenitor Yuwen Tai summoned Yuchi Jiong to court to comfort his mother.

sentences.zh: 遣大鴻臚郊勞，仍賜迥袞冕之服。

translations.literal: He dispatched the grand master of ceremonies to welcome him with suburban honors, and still granted Jiong robes of the highest ceremonial rank.
translations.idiomatic: He sent the grand master of ceremonies to welcome him with suburban honors and granted Yuchi Jiong the highest ceremonial robes.

sentences.zh: 蜀人思之，立碑頌德。

translations.literal: The people of Shu remembered him and erected a stele praising his virtue.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Shu remembered him and raised a stele in praise of his virtue.

sentences.zh: 孝閔踐阼，進位柱國大將軍。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, Jiong was advanced in rank to pillar of state and grand general.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin succeeded, Yuchi Jiong was raised to pillar of state and grand general.

sentences.zh: 又以迥有平蜀之功，同霍去病冠軍之義，封寧蜀公。

translations.literal: Also because Jiong had the merit of pacifying Shu, matching the meaning of Huo Qubing's title Champion, he was enfeoffed Duke of Ningshu.
translations.idiomatic: For pacifying Shu—an achievement likened to Huo Qubing's title Champion—he was enfeoffed Duke of Ningshu.

sentences.zh: 進蜀公，爵邑萬戶。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Duke of Shu, with a fief of ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: He was raised to Duke of Shu with a fief of ten thousand households.

sentences.zh: 宣帝即位，以迥為大前疑，出為相州總管。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan took the throne, Jiong was made grand mentor and sent out as governor-general of Xiang Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, Yuchi Jiong was made grand mentor and posted as governor-general of Xiang Province.

sentences.zh: 宣帝崩，隋文帝輔政，以迥望位夙重，懼為異圖，乃令迥子魏安公惇齎詔書以會葬徵迥。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan died, Yang Jian (Emperor Wen of Sui) assisted the government; because Jiong's reputation and rank had long been weighty, fearing he might harbor a different design, he ordered Jiong's son, Duke of Wei'an Dun, to carry an edict summoning Jiong on the pretext of attending the funeral.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Xuan's death Yang Jian, later Emperor Wen of Sui, took power as regent; fearing that Yuchi Jiong, long eminent in rank and reputation, might plot against him, he sent Jiong's son Dun, Duke of Wei'an, with an edict summoning Jiong to the capital for the funeral.

sentences.zh: 尋以鄖公韋孝寬代迥為總管。

translations.literal: Soon after, Duke of Yun Wei Xiaokuan was sent to replace Jiong as governor-general.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Wei Xiaokuan, Duke of Yun, was sent to replace Yuchi Jiong as governor-general.

sentences.zh: 迥以隋文帝當權，將圖篡奪，遂謀舉兵，留惇而不受代。

translations.literal: Jiong, because Yang Jian (Emperor Wen of Sui) held power and was about to usurp the throne, thereupon plotted to raise troops, kept Dun and refused to accept replacement.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing that Yang Jian held power and meant to seize the throne, Yuchi Jiong plotted rebellion, kept Dun with him, and refused to yield his post.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝又使候正破六汗裒詣迥喻旨，密與總管府長史晉昶等書，令為之備。

translations.literal: Yang Jian (Emperor Wen of Sui) also sent Houzheng Poliuhan Pu to Jiong to explain the imperial intent, and secretly wrote to the governor-general's chief administrator Jin Chang and others, ordering them to prepare.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian also sent Houzheng Poliuhan Pu to explain the court's wishes to Yuchi Jiong, and secretly wrote to chief administrator Jin Chang and others at the governor-general's office telling them to stand ready.

sentences.zh: 迥聞之，殺長史及裒。

translations.literal: When Jiong heard of it, he killed the chief administrator and Pu.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuchi Jiong learned of this, he killed the chief administrator and Pu.

sentences.zh: 乃集文武士庶，登城北樓而令之曰：「楊堅以凡庸之才，藉後父之勢，挾幼主而令天下，威福自己，賞罰無章，不臣之跡，暴於行路。

translations.literal: He thereupon assembled civil and military officials and common people, ascended the north city tower, and proclaimed to them: "Yang Jian, with commonplace talent, relying on the power of being father-in-law to the empress, holds the young lord and commands the realm; authority and favor are his alone, rewards and punishments without rule—the traces of disloyalty are exposed on the public road.
translations.idiomatic: He then gathered officials and commoners on the north city tower and declared: "Yang Jian is a man of ordinary gifts who rides the empress's father's power, controls the boy emperor, and rules as he pleases—reward and punishment are lawless, and his treason is plain for all on the road to see.

sentences.zh: 吾居將相，與國舅甥，同休共戚，義由一體。

translations.literal: I stand in the ranks of general and minister, and with the state's maternal uncle we are nephew and uncle; we share fortune and share woe—the righteousness binds us as one body.
translations.idiomatic: I am general and minister; with the imperial uncle we are kin by marriage—we share the same fate, bound as one body.

sentences.zh: 先帝處吾於此，本欲寄以安危。

translations.literal: The late emperor placed me here originally intending to entrust the realm's safety and peril to me.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor posted me here to entrust the realm's safety to my hands.

sentences.zh: 今欲與卿等糾合義勇，匡國庇人，進可以享榮名，退可以終臣節。

translations.literal: Now I wish together with you to gather righteous volunteers, set the state aright and shelter the people—advancing, one may enjoy glory and fame; retreating, one may preserve ministerial integrity to the end.
translations.idiomatic: Now I mean to rally loyal men with you to restore the dynasty and protect the people—advance, and we win honor; retreat, and we keep our loyalty intact.

sentences.zh: 卿等以為何如？

translations.literal: What do you think?"
translations.idiomatic: What say you?"

sentences.zh: 」於是衆咸從命，莫不感激。

translations.literal: " Thereupon the multitude all followed his command; none failed to be moved and inspired.
translations.idiomatic: " The crowd answered as one, every heart stirred.

sentences.zh: 乃自稱大總管，承制署置官司。

translations.literal: He thereupon styled himself grand governor-general, and by delegated imperial authority established and appointed official posts.
translations.idiomatic: He then proclaimed himself grand governor-general and, acting by delegated imperial authority, set up offices and appointments.

sentences.zh: 于時趙王招已入朝，留少子在國，迥又奉以號令。

translations.literal: At that time Prince of Zhao Zhao had already entered court, leaving a younger son in the realm; Jiong again upheld him in issuing orders.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Zhao Zhao was already at court, with a younger son left behind; Yuchi Jiong issued orders in the prince's name as well.

sentences.zh: 迥弟子勤，時為青州總管，亦從迥。

translations.literal: Jiong's younger brother's son Qin was then governor-general of Qing Province and also followed Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: Yuchi Jiong's nephew Qin, then governor-general of Qing Province, joined him too.

sentences.zh: 迥所管相、衛、黎、毛、洺、貝、趙、冀、瀛、滄，勤所統青、膠、光、莒諸州，皆從之。

translations.literal: The provinces Jiong administered—Xiang, Wei, Li, Mao, Ming, Bei, Zhao, Ji, Ying, and Cang—and the provinces Qin commanded—Qing, Jiao, Guang, and Ju—all followed him.
translations.idiomatic: The provinces under Yuchi Jiong—Xiang, Wei, Li, Mao, Ming, Bei, Zhao, Ji, Ying, and Cang—and those under Qin—Qing, Jiao, Guang, and Ju—all rose with him.

sentences.zh: 衆數十萬。

translations.literal: The host numbered several hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: His forces numbered in the hundreds of thousands.

sentences.zh: 滎州刺史邵公宇文冑、申州刺史李惠、東楚州刺史費也利進、東潼州刺史曹孝達，各據州以應迥。

translations.literal: Governor of Xing Province, Duke of Shao Yuwen Zhou; governor of Shen Province, Li Hui; governor of East Chu Province, Feiye Lijin; and governor of East Tong Province, Cao Xiaoda—each held his province in response to Jiong.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Zhou, Duke of Shao and governor of Xing Province; Li Hui of Shen Province; Feiye Lijin of East Chu Province; and Cao Xiaoda of East Tong Province each held his province for Yuchi Jiong.

sentences.zh: 迥又北結高寶寧以通突厥；

translations.literal: Jiong also allied in the north with Gao Baoning to reach the Turks;
translations.idiomatic: Yuchi Jiong also allied in the north with Gao Baoning to open contact with the Turks;

sentences.zh: 南連陳人，許割江、淮之地。

translations.literal: in the south he connected with the Chen people and promised to cede the lands of the Yangtze and Huai.
translations.idiomatic: in the south he treated with Chen and promised them the Yangtze and Huai regions.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝於是徵兵討迥，即以韋孝寬為元帥。

translations.literal: Yang Jian (Emperor Wen of Sui) thereupon mobilized troops to suppress Jiong, and immediately made Wei Xiaokuan commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian then raised armies against Yuchi Jiong and made Wei Xiaokuan supreme commander.

sentences.zh: 惇率衆十萬入武德，軍於沁東。

translations.literal: Dun led a host of one hundred thousand into Wude and encamped east of the Qin River.
translations.idiomatic: Dun led one hundred thousand men into Wude and camped east of the Qin River.

sentences.zh: 孝寬等諸軍隔水相持不進。

translations.literal: Wei Xiaokuan and the other armies faced each other across the water and did not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xiaokuan's armies faced them across the river and held back.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝又遣高熲馳驛督戰。

translations.literal: Yang Jian (Emperor Wen of Sui) also dispatched Gao Jiong by post-horse relay to supervise the battle.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian also sent Gao Jiong by relay horse to take command of the fighting.

sentences.zh: 惇布兵二十裏，麾軍小卻，欲待孝寬軍半度擊之。

translations.literal: Dun deployed his troops for twenty li, waved the army to fall back slightly, intending to wait until Wei Xiaokuan's army was half across and then strike.
translations.idiomatic: Dun drew up his line for twenty li, then feigned a slight withdrawal, planning to hit Wei Xiaokuan while half his force was still crossing.

sentences.zh: 孝寬因其小卻，鳴鼓齊進，惇大敗。

translations.literal: Wei Xiaokuan, taking advantage of his slight withdrawal, beat drums and advanced together; Dun was greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xiaokuan seized on the feigned retreat, sounded the drums, and charged in unison; Dun was routed.

sentences.zh: 孝寬乘勝進至鄴。

translations.literal: Wei Xiaokuan pressed the victory and advanced to Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xiaokuan pressed the victory on to Ye.

sentences.zh: 迥與子惇、佑等又悉其卒十三萬，陳于城南。

translations.literal: Jiong together with his sons Dun, You, and the others again mustered all their soldiers, one hundred thirty thousand, and drew up south of the city.
translations.idiomatic: Yuchi Jiong mustered all his remaining strength—one hundred thirty thousand men—and formed battle lines south of the city with his sons Dun, You, and the rest.

sentences.zh: 迥別統萬人，皆綠巾錦襖，號曰黃龍兵。

translations.literal: Jiong separately commanded ten thousand men, all with green headcloths and brocade jackets, styled the Yellow Dragon troops.
translations.idiomatic: Yuchi Jiong personally led ten thousand men in green headbands and brocade jackets, called the Yellow Dragon Army.

sentences.zh: 勤率衆五萬，自青州赴迥，以三千騎先到。

translations.literal: Qin led a host of fifty thousand from Qing Province to join Jiong; with three thousand cavalry he arrived first.
translations.idiomatic: Qin marched fifty thousand men from Qing Province to Yuchi Jiong's aid, his three thousand horse arriving first.

sentences.zh: 迥舊習軍旅，雖老猶被甲臨陣。

translations.literal: Jiong was long practiced in military affairs; though old he still donned armor and faced the battle line.
translations.idiomatic: Yuchi Jiong was a veteran of many campaigns; though aged, he still donned armor and took the field.

sentences.zh: 其麾下千兵，皆關中人，為之力戰。

translations.literal: The thousand soldiers under his command were all men of Guanzhong and fought hard for him.
translations.idiomatic: The thousand men under his personal command were all Guanzhong natives and fought for him with desperate courage.

sentences.zh: 孝寬等軍失利而卻。

translations.literal: Wei Xiaokuan and the other armies lost the battle and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Xiaokuan's army was beaten and fell back.

sentences.zh: 鄴中士女，觀者如堵。

translations.literal: Within Ye, men and women watching were thick as a wall.
translations.idiomatic: The men and women of Ye crowded the streets to watch, packed wall to wall.

sentences.zh: 高熲與李詢整陣，先犯觀者，因其擾而乘之。

translations.literal: Gao Jiong and Li Xun ordered the ranks and first drove into the spectators, then taking advantage of the disturbance pressed the attack.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Jiong and Li Xun formed their lines, first charged the spectators, and then exploited the chaos to press the attack.

sentences.zh: 迥大敗，遂入鄴。

translations.literal: Jiong was greatly defeated and thereupon entered Ye.
translations.idiomatic: Yuchi Jiong was routed and fled into Ye.

sentences.zh: 迥走保北城，孝寬縱兵圍之。

translations.literal: Jiong fled to hold the north city; Wei Xiaokuan released his troops to besiege it.
translations.idiomatic: Yuchi Jiong withdrew into the north city; Wei Xiaokuan unleashed his troops to besiege it.

sentences.zh: 李詢、賀樓子幹以其屬先登。

translations.literal: Li Xun and Helou Zigan with their followers were first to ascend.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xun and Helou Zigan were first over the wall with their men.

sentences.zh: 迥上樓，射殺數人，乃自殺。

translations.literal: Jiong ascended the tower, shot and killed several men, and then killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yuchi Jiong climbed the tower, shot down several men, and then took his own life.

sentences.zh: 勤、惇等東走，幷追獲之。

translations.literal: Qin, Dun, and the others fled east and were both pursued and captured.
translations.idiomatic: Qin, Dun, and the others fled east and were run down and captured.

sentences.zh: 餘衆，月餘皆斬之。

translations.literal: The remaining host, after more than a month, were all beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: The remaining troops were hunted down and beheaded over the next month.

sentences.zh: 迥末年衰耄，惑於後妻王氏，而諸子多不睦。

translations.literal: In his later years Jiong was declining and senile, deluded by his later wife, Lady Wang, while his sons for the most part were not harmonious.
translations.idiomatic: In his last years Yuchi Jiong had grown feeble and senile, bewitched by his second wife, Lady Wang, while his sons were largely at odds with one another.

sentences.zh: 以開府、小禦正崔達拏為長史，餘委任亦多用齊人。

translations.literal: He made opening-office, junior rectifier Cui Dana chief administrator; the rest of his appointments also largely used men of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: He made opening-office Cui Dana, junior rectifier, his chief administrator, and filled most other posts with men from Qi.

sentences.zh: 達拏文士，無籌略，舉措多失綱紀，不能有所匡救。

translations.literal: Dana was a literary man, without strategy or plan; in action he often lost the thread of law and order and could not set things aright.
translations.idiomatic: Dana was a scholar without strategic sense; his decisions repeatedly breached discipline, and he could not steer affairs back on course.

sentences.zh: 迥自起兵至敗，六十八日。

translations.literal: From the time Jiong raised troops until his defeat, sixty-eight days.
translations.idiomatic: From the day Jiong raised troops until his defeat, sixty-eight days passed.

sentences.zh: 武德中，迥從孫庫部員外郎耆福上表，請改葬。

translations.literal: In Wude, Jiong's collateral descendant Qifu, warden of the treasury section and exterior official, submitted a memorial requesting reburial.
translations.idiomatic: During Wude, Jiong's collateral descendant Qifu, a treasury-section exterior official, submitted a memorial asking that he be reburied.

sentences.zh: 朝議以迥忠於周室，有詔許之。

translations.literal: The court deliberated that Jiong had been loyal to the Zhou house, and an edict permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: The court held that Jiong had been loyal to the Zhou house, and an edict granted the request.

sentences.zh: 王謙字勑萬，太保雄之子也。

translations.literal: Wang Qian, styled Timo, was the son of Grand Guardian Xiong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Qian, styled Timo, was the son of Grand Guardian Wang Xiong.

sentences.zh: 性恭謹，無他才能。

translations.literal: By nature respectful and cautious, he had no other talents.
translations.idiomatic: Respectful and cautious by nature, he had no other special talents.

sentences.zh: 以父功，累遷驃騎大將軍、開府。

translations.literal: Through his father's merit, he was repeatedly promoted to grand general of rapid cavalry and opening-office commander.
translations.idiomatic: Through his father's merit he rose in stages to grand general of rapid cavalry and opening-office commander.

sentences.zh: 孝閔踐祚，治右小武伯。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xiaomin acceded, he served as director of the right minor martial guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin acceded, he served as director of the right minor martial guard.

sentences.zh: 雄從晉公護東討，為齊人所斃。

translations.literal: Xiong followed Duke of Jin Hu on an eastern campaign and was killed by Qi men.
translations.idiomatic: Xiong followed Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu on an eastern campaign and was killed by Northern Qi troops.

sentences.zh: 朝議以謙父殞身行陣，特加殊寵，乃授謙柱國大將軍。

translations.literal: The court deliberated that Qian's father had died on the battlefield and, granting exceptional favor, appointed Qian pillar-of-state grand general.
translations.idiomatic: The court held that Qian's father had fallen on the battlefield and, as a special honor, appointed Qian pillar-of-state grand general.

sentences.zh: 以情禮未終，固辭不拜。

translations.literal: Because the period of mourning affection had not ended, he firmly declined the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: Because his mourning obligations were not yet complete, he firmly declined the appointment.

sentences.zh: 高祖手詔奪情，襲爵庸公，邑萬戶。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu wrote a personal edict overriding mourning obligations; he inherited the title Duke of Yong with a fief of ten thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu issued a personal edict overriding mourning obligations, and Qian inherited the title Duke of Yong with a fief of ten thousand households.

translations.literal: (Later)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: later]

sentences.zh: 〔從〕皇太子討吐谷渾，力戰有功。

translations.literal: [From] the crown prince against Tuyuhun, he fought hard and had merit.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the crown prince against Tuyuhun, fought hard, and won distinction.

sentences.zh: 是時高祖東征，謙又力戰，進上柱國、益州總管。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Gaozu campaigned east, and Qian again fought hard; he was promoted to upper pillar of state and inspector-general of Yi Province.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu campaigned east, Qian again fought hard and was promoted to upper pillar of state and inspector-general of Yi Province.

sentences.zh: 時〔隋文帝秉政〕，謙令司錄賀若昂奉表詣闕。

translations.literal: At that time [Yang Jian held government power], Qian ordered chief clerk He Ruo'ang to present a memorial at court.
translations.idiomatic: At that time, with Yang Jian directing the government, Qian ordered chief clerk He Ruo'ang to present a memorial at court.

sentences.zh: 昂還，具陳京師事勢。

translations.literal: When Ang returned, he fully reported the situation in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When He Ruo'ang returned, he gave a full account of affairs in the capital.

sentences.zh: 謙以世受國恩，將圖匡復，遂舉兵，署官司。

translations.literal: Qian, having received the state's grace generation after generation, intended to restore the dynasty, and so raised troops and appointed offices.
translations.idiomatic: Qian, having received the state's grace for generations, intended to restore the dynasty, raised troops, and appointed officials.

sentences.zh: 所管益、潼、新、始、龍、邛、青、瀘、戎、寧、汶、陵、遂、合、楚、資、眉、普十八州及嘉、渝、臨、渠、蓬、隆、通、興、武、庸十州之人多從之。

translations.literal: The people of the eighteen provinces under his charge—Yi, Tong, Xin, Shi, Long, Qiong, Qing, Lu, Rong, Ning, Wen, Ling, Sui, He, Chu, Zi, Mei, and Pu—and the ten additional prefectures of Jia, Yu, Lin, Qu, Peng, Long, Tong, Xing, Wu, and Yong largely followed him.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the eighteen provinces and ten additional prefectures under his jurisdiction—Yi, Tong, Xin, Shi, Long, Qiong, Qing, Lu, Rong, Ning, Wen, Ling, Sui, He, Chu, Zi, Mei, Pu, Jia, Yu, Lin, Qu, Peng, Long, Tong, Xing, Wu, and Yong—largely rallied to him.

sentences.zh: 總管長史乙弗虔、益州刺史達奚惎勸謙據險觀變。

translations.literal: Chief administrator Yifu Qian and Yi Governor Daxi Ji urged Qian to hold the difficult terrain and watch how events unfolded.
translations.idiomatic: Chief administrator Yifu Qian and Yi governor Daxi Ji urged Wang Qian to hold the difficult terrain and wait to see how events developed.

sentences.zh: 隆州刺史〔高〕阿

translations.literal: Governor of Long Province [Gao] A
translations.idiomatic: Long Province governor Gao A

translations.literal: (Shi)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: Shi]

sentences.zh: 那瑰為謙畫三策曰：「公親率精銳，直指散關，蜀人知公有勤王之節，必當各思效命，此上策也；

translations.literal: Na Gui drew up three plans for Qian, saying: "My lord, leading picked troops yourself and striking straight for San Gate Pass—the Shu people, knowing you have the loyalty of one who rushes to aid the sovereign, will surely each think to give their lives; this is the highest plan;
translations.idiomatic: Na Gui proposed three plans to Qian: "If you personally lead picked troops straight for San Gate Pass, the people of Shu, knowing your loyalty in rushing to aid the throne, will surely each resolve to serve you—this is the best plan;

sentences.zh: 出兵梁、漢，以顧天下，此中策也；

translations.literal: to send troops from Liang and Han and thereby command the realm's attention—this is the middle plan;
translations.idiomatic: to send troops from Liang and Han and thereby hold the realm's attention—this is the middle plan;

sentences.zh: 坐守劔南，發兵自衛，此下策也。

translations.literal: to sit and hold Jiannan and raise troops only for self-defense—this is the lowest plan.
translations.idiomatic: to sit in Jiannan and raise troops only for self-defense—this is the worst plan.

sentences.zh: 」謙參用其中下之策。

translations.literal: " Qian partly adopted the middle and lower plans.
translations.idiomatic: " Qian adopted parts of the middle and lower plans.

sentences.zh: 梁睿未至大劔，謙遣兵鎮始州。

translations.literal: Before Liang Rui reached Great Sword Pass, Qian sent troops to garrison Shi Province.
translations.idiomatic: Before Liang Rui reached Great Sword Pass, Qian sent troops to garrison Shi Province.

sentences.zh: 隋文即以睿為行軍元帥，便發利、鳳、文、秦、成諸州兵討之。

translations.literal: Yang Jian immediately made Rui campaign commander-in-chief and dispatched troops from Li, Feng, Wen, Qin, Cheng, and other provinces to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian immediately made Liang Rui campaign commander-in-chief and dispatched troops from Li, Feng, Wen, Qin, Cheng, and other provinces against him.

sentences.zh: 達奚惎、乙弗虔等衆十萬攻利州。

translations.literal: Daxi Ji, Yifu Qian, and others with a host of one hundred thousand attacked Li Province.
translations.idiomatic: Daxi Ji, Yifu Qian, and others with a host of one hundred thousand attacked Li Province.

sentences.zh: 聞睿至，衆潰。

translations.literal: When they heard Rui had arrived, the host broke up.
translations.idiomatic: When they heard Rui had arrived, the army broke apart.

sentences.zh: 睿乘其弊，縱兵深入。

translations.literal: Rui seized their weakness and drove his troops in deep.
translations.idiomatic: Rui seized their weakness and drove his troops deep into the country.

sentences.zh: 惎、虔密使詣睿，請為內應以贖罪。

translations.literal: Ji and Qian secretly sent envoys to Rui asking to serve as inner allies to redeem their guilt.
translations.idiomatic: Ji and Qian secretly sent envoys to Rui offering to serve as inside allies to atone for their guilt.

sentences.zh: 謙不知之，並令守成都。

translations.literal: Qian knew nothing of this and still ordered them to hold Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Qian knew nothing of this and still ordered them to hold Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 謙先無籌略，承藉父勳，遂居重任。

translations.literal: Qian had no strategy from the start; relying on his father's merit, he had risen to a weighty post.
translations.idiomatic: Qian had no strategy to begin with; relying on his father's merit, he had risen to a weighty post.

sentences.zh: 初謀舉兵，咸以地有江山之險，進可以立功，退可以自守。

translations.literal: When they first planned to rebel, all held that the land had the defenses of rivers and mountains—advancing one could win merit, retreating one could hold oneself.
translations.idiomatic: When they first planned rebellion, all held that the land was defended by rivers and mountains—one could win glory by advancing and hold out by retreating.

sentences.zh: 且任用多非其才。

translations.literal: Moreover, those appointed were mostly not men of the right talent.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, most of those he appointed were not men of real ability.

sentences.zh: 及聞睿兵奄至，惶懼，乃自率衆迎戰。

translations.literal: When he heard Rui's troops had suddenly arrived, he was afraid and personally led his host to meet them in battle.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard Rui's army had suddenly arrived, he was terrified and personally led his troops out to fight.

sentences.zh: 又以惎、虔之子為左右軍。

translations.literal: He also made Ji and Qian's sons command the left and right wings.
translations.idiomatic: He also made Ji's and Qian's sons command the left and right wings.

sentences.zh: 行數十里，軍皆叛。

translations.literal: After marching several tens of li, the army all turned against him.
translations.idiomatic: After marching several tens of li, the whole army turned against him.

sentences.zh: 謙以二十騎奔新都，縣令王寶斬之，傳首京師。

translations.literal: Qian fled to Xindu with twenty horsemen; Magistrate Wang Bao beheaded him and sent his head to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Qian fled to Xindu with twenty horsemen; Magistrate Wang Bao beheaded him and sent his head to the capital.

sentences.zh: 惎、虔以成都降，隋文以其首謀，斬之。

translations.literal: Ji and Qian surrendered Chengdu; Yang Jian, because they had been the chief plotters, beheaded them.
translations.idiomatic: Ji and Qian surrendered Chengdu; Yang Jian, judging them the chief plotters, had them beheaded.

sentences.zh: 〔高〕阿

translations.literal: [Gao] A
translations.idiomatic: Gao A

translations.literal: (Shi)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: Shi]

sentences.zh: 那瑰亦誅。

translations.literal: Na Gui was also executed.
translations.idiomatic: Na Gui was also executed.

sentences.zh: 司馬消難字道融，河內溫人。

translations.literal: Sima Xiaonan, styled Daorong, was a man of Wen in Henei.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Xiaonan, styled Daorong, was a native of Wen in Henei.

sentences.zh: 父子如，為齊神武佐命，位至尚書令。

translations.literal: His father Ziru assisted Gao Huan of Northern Qi at the founding and rose to director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sima Ziru had assisted Gao Huan at the founding of Northern Qi and rose to director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 消難幼聰惠，微涉經史，好自矯飾，以求名譽。

translations.literal: Xiaonan was clever from youth, lightly touched on the classics and histories, liked to adorn himself, and sought reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaonan was clever from youth, had a light acquaintance with the classics and histories, liked to polish his appearance, and sought reputation.

sentences.zh: 起家著作郎。

translations.literal: He began his career as a gentleman-attendant compiler.
translations.idiomatic: He began his career as a gentleman-attendant compiler.

sentences.zh: 子如旣當朝貴，消難亦愛賓客。

translations.literal: Once Ziru held court rank and power, Xiaonan also cultivated guests.
translations.idiomatic: Once Ziru held high court rank, Xiaonan also cultivated guests.

sentences.zh: 邢子才、王元景、魏收、陸卬、崔贍等皆遊其門。

translations.literal: Xing Zicai, Wang Yuanjing, Wei Shou, Lu Yang, Cui Zhan, and others all frequented his gate.
translations.idiomatic: Xing Zicai, Wang Yuanjing, Wei Shou, Lu Yang, Cui Zhan, and others all frequented his house.

sentences.zh: 尋拜駙馬都尉、光祿卿，出為北豫州刺史。

translations.literal: He was soon appointed commandant of the horse guard and director of imperial feasts, and sent out as governor of North Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made commandant of the horse guard and director of imperial feasts, then sent out as governor of North Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 齊文宣末年，昬虐滋甚。

translations.literal: In the last years of Emperor Wenxuan of Qi, his cruelty and tyranny grew ever worse.
translations.idiomatic: In the last years of Emperor Wenxuan of Qi, his cruelty and tyranny grew ever worse.

sentences.zh: 消難旣懼禍及，常有自全之謀，曲意撫納，頗為百姓所附。

translations.literal: Xiaonan, fearing calamity would reach him, constantly plotted to preserve himself; he courted favor and won over the people and was much attached to by the common folk.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaonan, fearing disaster would reach him, constantly plotted to save himself; he courted favor, won over the people, and gained a strong local following.

sentences.zh: 屬文宣在幷，驛召其弟上黨王渙，渙懼于屠害，遂斬使者東奔。

translations.literal: When Wenxuan was at Bing, he summoned by post his brother the Prince of Shangdang, Huan; Huan, fearing slaughter, slew the messenger and fled east.
translations.idiomatic: When Wenxuan was at Bing, he summoned by courier his brother the Prince of Shangdang, Huan; Huan, fearing slaughter, killed the messenger and fled east.

sentences.zh: 數日間搜捕鄴中，鄴中大擾。

translations.literal: Within several days Ye was searched and hunted; Ye was greatly disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few days Ye was searched and hunted, and the city was thrown into turmoil.

sentences.zh: 後竟獲於濟州。

translations.literal: Later he was finally captured in Ji Province.
translations.idiomatic: He was finally captured in Ji Province.

sentences.zh: 渙之初走，朝士私相謂曰：「今上黨亡叛，似赴成皋。

translations.literal: When Huan first fled, court gentlemen said privately to one another: "Now the Prince of Shangdang has fled in rebellion, as if heading for Chenggao.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan first fled, courtiers said privately among themselves: "The Prince of Shangdang has fled in rebellion, as if heading for Chenggao.

sentences.zh: 若與司馬北豫州連謀，必為國患。

translations.literal: If he joins in conspiracy with Sima of North Yu Province, he will surely become a threat to the state.
translations.idiomatic: If he joins in conspiracy with Sima Xiaonan of North Yu Province, he will surely become a threat to the state.

sentences.zh: 」此言遂達於文宣，文宣頗疑之。

translations.literal: " This talk reached Wenxuan, and he grew quite suspicious.
translations.idiomatic: " This talk reached Wenxuan, and he grew deeply suspicious.

sentences.zh: 消難懼，密令所親裴藻間行入關，請舉州來附。

translations.literal: Xiaonan was afraid; he secretly ordered his close associate Pei Zao to slip across the border into the Pass region and ask to surrender the entire province.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaonan was afraid; he secretly ordered his close associate Pei Zao to slip into the Pass region and ask to surrender the entire province.

sentences.zh: 晉公護遣達奚武、楊忠迎之，消難遂與武俱入朝。

translations.literal: Duke of Jin Hu dispatched Daxi Wu and Yang Zhong to welcome him; Xiaonan thereupon entered court together with Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Duke of Jin Yuwen Hu sent Daxi Wu and Yang Zhong to welcome him; Xiaonan then entered court together with Wu.

sentences.zh: 授大將軍、滎陽公。

translations.literal: He was appointed grand general and Duke of Xingyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed grand general and Duke of Xingyang.

sentences.zh: 從高祖東伐，遷大後丞。

translations.literal: He followed Emperor Gaozu on the eastern campaign and was transferred to grand rear chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Emperor Gaozu on the eastern campaign and was transferred to grand rear chancellor.

sentences.zh: 納女為靜帝后。

translations.literal: He gave his daughter in marriage as empress to Emperor Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He gave his daughter in marriage as empress to Emperor Jing.

sentences.zh: 尋出為

translations.literal: Soon he was sent out as
translations.idiomatic: He was soon sent out as

translations.literal: (Jiao)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: Jiao]

sentences.zh: ［鄖］州總管。

translations.literal: [Yun] inspector-general.
translations.idiomatic: inspector-general of Yun Province.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝輔政，消難旣聞蜀公迥不受代，遂欲與迥合勢，亦舉兵應之。

translations.literal: When Yang Jian directed the government, Xiaonan, having heard that Duke of Shu Jiong refused to be replaced, intended to join forces with Jiong and also raised troops in response.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Jian directed the government, Xiaonan, hearing that Duke of Shu Jiong refused to be replaced, intended to join forces with him and also raised troops in response.

sentences.zh: 以開府田廣等為腹心，殺總管長史侯莫陳杲、鄖州刺史蔡澤等四十餘人。

translations.literal: Taking opening-office commanders Tian Guang and others as his inner circle, he killed chief administrator Houmochen Gao, Yun Governor Cai Ze, and more than forty others.
translations.idiomatic: Taking opening-office commanders Tian Guang and others as his inner circle, he killed chief administrator Houmochen Gao, Yun governor Cai Ze, and more than forty others.

sentences.zh: 所管鄖、隨、溫、應

translations.literal: The nine provinces under his charge—Yun, Sui, Wen, Ying
translations.idiomatic: The nine provinces under his charge—Yun, Sui, Wen, Ying

translations.literal: (Shi)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: Shi]

sentences.zh: 〔土〕、順、沔、環、岳九州，魯山、甑山、沌陽、應城、平靖、武陽、上明、

translations.literal: [Tu], Shun, Mian, Huan, and Yue, and the eight garrisons of Lushan, Zengshan, Chunyang, Yingcheng, Pingjing, Wuyang, Shaming, and
translations.idiomatic: Tu, Shun, Mian, Huan, and Yue, and the eight garrisons of Lushan, Zengshan, Chunyang, Yingcheng, Pingjing, Wuyang, Shaming, and

translations.literal: (Xu)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: Xu]

sentences.zh: 〔溳〕水八鎮，並從之。

translations.literal: [Yun]shui—all followed him.
translations.idiomatic: Yunshui—all followed him.

sentences.zh: 使其子泳質於陳以求援。

translations.literal: He sent his son Yong as a hostage to Chen to seek aid.
translations.idiomatic: He sent his son Yong as a hostage to Chen to seek aid.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝命襄州總管王誼為元帥，發荊襄兵以討之。

translations.literal: Yang Jian ordered Yun Inspector-General Wang Yi as commander-in-chief and dispatched Jing-Xiang troops to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian ordered Wang Yi, inspector-general of Xiang, as commander-in-chief and dispatched Jing-Xiang troops to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 八月，消難聞誼軍將至，夜率其麾下，歸於陳。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, hearing Yi's army was about to arrive, Xiaonan by night led his personal followers and went over to Chen.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, hearing Wang Yi's army was about to arrive, Xiaonan led his personal followers by night and defected to Chen.

sentences.zh: 陳宣帝以為都督安

translations.literal: Emperor Xuan of Chen made him commander of An
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xuan of Chen made him commander of An

translations.literal: (Zhao)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: Zhao]

sentences.zh: 〔隨〕九州八鎮、車騎將軍、司空、隨公。

translations.literal: [Sui], the nine provinces and eight garrisons, plus general of chariots and cavalry, minister of works, and Duke of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Sui, the nine provinces and eight garrisons, plus general of chariots and cavalry, minister of works, and Duke of Sui.

sentences.zh: 初，楊忠之迎消難，結為兄弟，情好甚篤。

translations.literal: At first, when Yang Zhong welcomed Xiaonan, they became sworn brothers and their affection was very deep.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Zhong first welcomed Xiaonan, they became sworn brothers and were deeply attached.

sentences.zh: 隋文每以叔禮事之。

translations.literal: Yang Jian always treated him with the courtesy due an uncle.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jian always treated him with the courtesy due an uncle.

sentences.zh: 及陳平，消難至京，特免死，配為樂戶。

translations.literal: When Chen was pacified, Xiaonan reached the capital; he was specially spared death and assigned to the musicians' households.
translations.idiomatic: When Chen was pacified, Xiaonan reached the capital; he was specially spared death and assigned to the musicians' households.

sentences.zh: 經二旬放免。

translations.literal: After twenty days he was released.
translations.idiomatic: After twenty days he was released.

sentences.zh: 猶被舊恩，特蒙引見。

translations.literal: Still owing to past favor, he was specially granted an audience.
translations.idiomatic: Still owing to past favor, he was specially granted an audience.

sentences.zh: 尋卒于家。

translations.literal: Soon he died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He soon died at home.

sentences.zh: 性貪淫，輕於去就。

translations.literal: By nature he was greedy and licentious, and light in his coming and going.
translations.idiomatic: Greedy and licentious by nature, he was fickle in his loyalties.

sentences.zh: 故世之言反覆者，皆引消難云。

translations.literal: Thus when later ages speak of the fickle, they all cite Xiaonan.
translations.idiomatic: Thus when later ages speak of the fickle, they all cite Xiaonan.

sentences.zh: 其妻高氏，齊神武之女。

translations.literal: His wife, the Lady Gao, was a daughter of Gao Huan.
translations.idiomatic: His wife, Lady Gao, was a daughter of Gao Huan.

sentences.zh: 在鄴，敬重之。

translations.literal: In Ye he treated her with respect.
translations.idiomatic: In Ye he treated her with respect.

sentences.zh: 後入關，便相弃薄。

translations.literal: After entering the Pass region, he cast her off and treated her coldly.
translations.idiomatic: After entering the Pass region, he cast her off and treated her coldly.

sentences.zh: 消難之赴

translations.literal: When Xiaonan went to
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaonan went to

translations.literal: (Ang)
translations.idiomatic: [variant: Ang]

sentences.zh: 〔鄖〕州，留高及三子在京。

translations.literal: [Yun] Province, he left Lady Gao and three sons in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yun Province, he left Lady Gao and three sons in the capital.

sentences.zh: 高言於隋文曰：「滎陽公性多變詐，今以新寵自隨，必不顧妻子，願防慮之。

translations.literal: Lady Gao said to Yang Jian: "The Duke of Xingyang's nature is full of change and deceit; now that new favorites accompany him, he will surely not care for wife and children—I beg you to guard against this.
translations.idiomatic: Lady Gao said to Yang Jian: "The Duke of Xingyang is changeable and deceitful; now that new favorites accompany him, he will surely abandon wife and children—I beg you to guard against this.

sentences.zh: 」消難入陳，而高母子因此獲免。

translations.literal: " When Xiaonan entered Chen, Lady Gao and her sons were thereby spared.
translations.idiomatic: " When Xiaonan defected to Chen, Lady Gao and her sons were thereby spared.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：尉遲迥地則舅甥，職惟台袞，沐恩累葉，荷睠一時，居形勝之地，受藩維之托，顛而不扶，憂責斯在。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Weichi Jiong by kinship was nephew to the emperor; in office he held the highest ministerial rank; generation after generation he bathed in grace and for a time bore the sovereign's favor; he occupied commanding ground and received the trust of a frontier guardian—when the dynasty tottered he did not hold it up, and the burden of worry was his to bear.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Weichi Jiong was the emperor's nephew by marriage; in office he held the highest ministerial rank; generation after generation he bathed in grace and for a time bore the sovereign's favor; he occupied commanding ground and received the trust of a frontier guardian—when the dynasty tottered he did not hold it up, and the burden of worry was his to bear.

sentences.zh: 及主威云謝，鼎業將遷，九服移心，三靈改卜，遂能志存赴蹈，投袂稱兵。

translations.literal: When the sovereign's prestige faded like departing clouds and the dynastic foundation was about to shift, when the nine domains changed heart and the three spirits sought a new fortune, he could still resolve to rush forward and, throwing up his sleeves, raise arms.
translations.idiomatic: When the sovereign's prestige faded like departing clouds and the dynastic foundation was about to shift, when the nine domains changed heart and the three spirits sought a new fortune, he could still resolve to rush forward and, throwing up his sleeves, raise arms.

sentences.zh: 忠君之勤未宣，違天之禍便及。

translations.literal: His loyalty to the sovereign was not yet proclaimed when the calamity of defying Heaven fell upon him.
translations.idiomatic: His loyalty to the sovereign had not yet been proclaimed when the calamity of defying Heaven fell upon him.

sentences.zh: 校其心，翟義、葛誕之儔歟。

translations.literal: Weigh his heart—is he not of the company of Zhai Yi and Ge Dan?
translations.idiomatic: Weigh his heart—is he not of the company of Zhai Yi and Ge Dan?

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七一年十一月版《周書》為本校。

translations.literal: The entire text uses the Zhonghua Shuju, November 1971 edition of the Book of Zhou, as the base for this collation.
translations.idiomatic: This text was collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the 《Book of Zhou》 (November 1971).
